goal: Extract the attribute/protocol management responsibility from Safelist into a new class (SafelistAttributes) so that Safelist's public API surface and internal method count are reduced and the code for attribute, enforced-attribute and protocol handling is encapsulated in a cohesive component.

expected_impact.rationale: Moves the cohesive cluster of public attribute/protocol management methods (addAttributes, removeAttributes, addEnforcedAttribute, removeEnforcedAttribute, addProtocols, removeProtocols, isSafeAttribute, getEnforcedAttributes) plus three private helper methods (getProtocolValue, isSafeProtocol, isValidAnchor) and three large maps (attributes, enforcedAttributes, protocols) into a new class. This directly reduces Safelist's public method count by 8 and reduces total methods/LOC by moving the implementation out of the class into a dedicated component.

ops.details: Create a new production class org.jsoup.safety.SafelistAttributes in the same package. The new class will encapsulate the attribute/protocol responsibility and contain the following moved state and behavior: fields Map<TagName, Set<AttributeKey>> attributes; Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, AttributeValue>> enforcedAttributes; Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, Set<Protocol>>> protocols. Public API to be moved: addAttributes(String, String...), removeAttributes(String, String...), addEnforcedAttribute(String, String, String), removeEnforcedAttribute(String, String), addProtocols(String, String, String...), removeProtocols(String, String, String...), isSafeAttribute(String tagName, Element el, Attribute attr), getEnforcedAttributes(String tagName). Private helpers moved into the new class: getProtocolValue(Element, Attribute), isSafeProtocol(String, Set<Protocol>), isValidAnchor(String). The new class will reference the nested types as Safelist.TagName, Safelist.AttributeKey, Safelist.AttributeValue, Safelist.Protocol (these are static nested types in Safelist and remain in Safelist). Provide constructors: a default constructor and a copy constructor that accepts another SafelistAttributes instance to support Safelist(Safelist) copy. The extraction preserves behavior by moving implementation wholesale and exposing the same semantics via the new class. Safelist will keep tagNames, preserveRelativeLinks and higher-level responsibilities and hold a private final SafelistAttributes attributeManager to which attribute-related calls are delegated or which is used internally; internal call sites in Safelist will be updated to use the new class directly (no compatibility wrappers for moved public methods are kept in Safelist).
Move the field 'attributes' (Map<TagName, Set<AttributeKey>>) from Safelist into SafelistAttributes to own allowed-attributes state.
Move the field 'enforcedAttributes' (Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, AttributeValue>>) from Safelist into SafelistAttributes to own enforced-attributes state.
Move the field 'protocols' (Map<TagName, Map<AttributeKey, Set<Protocol>>>) from Safelist into SafelistAttributes to own protocol validation state.

Move public method addAttributes(String tag, String... attributes) into SafelistAttributes; implementation will operate on the moved 'attributes' map and return SafelistAttributes for chaining (or maintain original method chaining semantics by returning SafelistAttributes). Safelist will update its API uses to call attributeManager.addAttributes(...) where needed.
Move public method removeAttributes(String tag, String... attributes) into SafelistAttributes; adjust logic for :all handling within the new class.

Move public method addEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute, String value) into SafelistAttributes; implementation will maintain semantics and add tag to Safelist.tagNames if needed via a Safelist-visible API or Safelist will call tagNames.add separately where required. The new class will be responsible for storing enforcedAttributes.
Move public method removeEnforcedAttribute(String tag, String attribute) into SafelistAttributes; implementation removes entries from enforcedAttributes map.
Move public method addProtocols(String tag, String attribute, String... protocols) into SafelistAttributes; implementation will operate on the moved 'protocols' map and create Protocol objects.
Move public method removeProtocols(String tag, String attribute, String... removeProtocols) into SafelistAttributes; maintain validations and map cleanup semantics.

Move public method isSafeAttribute(String tagName, Element el, Attribute attr) into SafelistAttributes; it will use the moved maps and the private helpers (also moved) to evaluate attribute safety. It will continue to fall back to ':all' logic by invoking its own isSafeAttribute for ':all' when needed.
Move public method getEnforcedAttributes(String tagName) into SafelistAttributes; this builds and returns a org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes based on the enforcedAttributes map.
Move private helper getProtocolValue(Element el, Attribute attr) into SafelistAttributes to support protocol checks. It uses el.absUrl(...) and attr.getValue().
Move private helper isSafeProtocol(String value, Set<Protocol> protocols) into SafelistAttributes. Uses Normalizer.lowerCase and the Protocol typed values; retains the anchor '#' handling.
Move private static helper isValidAnchor(String value) into SafelistAttributes to centralize protocol anchor validation logic.

Add required imports to the new SafelistAttributes (org.jsoup.nodes.Element, org.jsoup.nodes.Attribute, org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes, java.util.*) and update Safelist imports if necessary. Ensure fully qualified references to nested types remain correct (use Safelist.TagName etc. from the new class).

Update internal references in Safelist to use the new SafelistAttributes instance (attributeManager). Remove the moved methods and fields from Safelist. Update the Safelist() constructor to initialize attributeManager, and the Safelist(Safelist copy) copy-constructor to copy attributeManager via its copy constructor. Update any call sites inside Safelist that previously used the moved private helpers or maps to delegate to attributeManager. Keep Safelist.TagName, AttributeKey, AttributeValue, Protocol and TypedValue nested types in Safelist so the new class references them as Safelist.TagName etc.

Update related tests affected by this refactoring block so the configured build command passes. Adjust imports, package references, moved class references, constructors, and assertions only when required. Do not change production behavior through tests.
